summary:
October  


I fail to find any evidence that I wrote to thank you for the pictures of the pretty girl. If I did write, then consider this letter an extension of my thanks. If I did not, then thank you. She really is pretty. 

By the way—I met a pretty lady last week: the director of a crew here from Paris to do a two-hour TV documentary on science fiction writers. I sort of fell in love with her, which is awkward, considering that I am married. My wife there­ upon left me, taking both the baby and the car. Thus is one paid for one’s trans- 
gressions, I guess, especially in view of the fact that she dented the fender back­ ing out of the garage. 

This French chick really is beyond belief, though. Her name is Elizabeth Antebi. Maybe she’ll visit your country someday. She is supposed to come back here in February with a print of the film. I’m afraid my marriage will stagger once more, but even so I can hardly wait. 

In other news, I sold DO ANDROIDS DREAM OF ELECTRIC SHEEP? to the movies: $2,000 option money and $25,000 if they go ahead and make it. This will be the most money I will have made. 

I have the galleys of FLOW MY TEARS, THE POLICEMAN SAID, so it will be coming out soon (February). Among the cuts I’m making, is to remove the name of an ex-girlfriend. I find I don’t even dislike her any longer, let alone love her.
